# Vercel Provider

The Vercel provider is used to interact with resources supported by Vercel.
The provider needs to be configured with the proper credentials before it can be used.

Use the navigation to the left to read about the available resources.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Configure the Vercel provider using the required_providers stanza.
# You may optionally use a version directive to prevent breaking
# changes occurring unannounced.
terraform {
  required_providers {
    vercel = {
      source  = "vercel/vercel"
      version = ">= 4.8"
    }
  }
}

provider "vercel" {
  # Or omit this for the api_token to be read
  # from the VERCEL_API_TOKEN environment variable
  api_token = var.vercel_api_token

  # Optional default team for all resources
  team = "your_team_slug_or_id"
}
```

## Authenticating with OIDC

Instead of a long-lived `api_token`, the provider can authenticate with an OIDC token issued by an external identity provider, such as your CI/CD provider. The provider exchanges it for a short-lived Vercel access token, so there is no Vercel secret to store or rotate.

The team needs an OIDC federation policy for the Vercel CLI that matches the issuer and claims of the OIDC token. Create it from the team's Build and Deployment settings, or with the `vercel_oidc_federation_policy` resource using `client = "vercel"`. The permissions of the policy decide what the provider can manage. They must include `read:team`, which the provider needs to look up the team.

Then give the OIDC token to the provider with `oidc_token` or `oidc_token_file_path`, and set `team` to the team of the policy:

```terraform
provider "vercel" {
  # Or omit this for the path to be read from the
  # VERCEL_TERRAFORM_OIDC_TOKEN_FILE_PATH environment variable
  oidc_token_file_path = "/var/run/secrets/tokens/vercel"

  # The team whose OIDC federation policy matches the token
  team = "your_team_slug_or_id"
}
```

The access token is short-lived. The provider exchanges the OIDC token again shortly before the access token expires, which only works while the OIDC token is itself still valid: after that, the run fails when the access token expires. GitHub Actions OIDC tokens, for example, are valid for about 5 minutes. For longer runs, use `oidc_token_file_path` with a file that is kept up to date, which the provider reads again on every exchange.

When authenticating with OIDC:

- The access token only gives access to the team set in `team`. To manage several teams, create a policy on each team and use one provider configuration per team.
- The access token belongs to the Vercel CLI app rather than to a user. Vercel API endpoints that require a user, such as the ones behind `vercel_oidc_federation_policy`, reject it.
- Prefer the environment variables to Terraform variables for the OIDC token. Terraform saves variable values in plan files, so applying a saved plan would exchange the OIDC token from the time of the plan, which may have expired.
- Environment variables are only read when the provider configuration sets none of `api_token`, `oidc_token` and `oidc_token_file_path`. `VERCEL_API_TOKEN` takes precedence over the OIDC ones, and the provider warns when both are set.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `api_token` (String, Sensitive) The Vercel API Token to use. This can also be specified with the `VERCEL_API_TOKEN` shell environment variable. Tokens can be created from your [Vercel settings](https://vercel.com/account/tokens).
- `oidc_policy_id` (String) The ID of the OIDC federation policy to exchange the OIDC token with. Only needed when more than one policy of the team matches the token. This can also be specified with the `VERCEL_TERRAFORM_OIDC_POLICY_ID` shell environment variable.
- `oidc_token` (String, Sensitive) An OIDC token issued by an external identity provider, such as your CI/CD provider, to exchange for a short-lived Vercel access token instead of using an `api_token`. This can also be specified with the `VERCEL_TERRAFORM_OIDC_TOKEN` shell environment variable. Requires `team`, and an OIDC federation policy for the Vercel CLI on that team that matches the token.
- `oidc_token_file_path` (String) The path to a file containing the OIDC token to exchange for a short-lived Vercel access token. The file is read again every time the access token is about to expire, so prefer it over `oidc_token` when the OIDC token is rotated during a run. This can also be specified with the `VERCEL_TERRAFORM_OIDC_TOKEN_FILE_PATH` shell environment variable.
- `team` (String) The default Vercel Team to use when creating resources or reading data sources. This can be provided as either a team slug, or team ID. The slug and ID are both available from the Team Settings page in the Vercel dashboard.
